essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions shaped the crisis by dividing Europe into competing blocs and raising fear of a wider war.
The Sarajevo assassination led through the July Crisis to declarations of war as alliance commitments and mobilization decisions spread the conflict.
From 1914 to 1918, the war moved from outbreak to U.S. entry and then to the armistice in a simple sequence.

activities.label: model
activities.title: European tensions and alliances
activities.body: Read the model and then move on.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions shaped the crisis by dividing Europe into competing blocs and raising fear of a wider war.

activities.label: explain
activities.title: Explain the alliance pattern
activities.body: In your own words, explain the alliance blocs and why they mattered. Keep it short and specific.
activities.correctAnswer: Europe was divided into rival alliance blocs, which made leaders fear that any local crisis could become a larger war.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the competing blocs and links them to wider-war fear. If needed, add one or two tensions that made the blocs dangerous.

activities.label: repair
activities.title: Fix the outbreak chain
activities.body: Use the correction cue to improve your answer. Then give one revised version.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Treating the assassination as the only cause, instead of the spark that moved through the July Crisis and mobilization decisions into war
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination was the spark, but the July Crisis, alliance commitments, and mobilization decisions turned it into declarations of war.
activities.feedback: The key fix is to separate the spark from the spread. The assassination starts the chain, but the war declarations come after the crisis, alliances, and mobilization.

activities.title: WWI from start to armistice
activities.body: Read the second model and then continue.

activities.label: recognize
activities.title: Place the war timeline
activities.body: Choose the best order for the main WWI milestones.
choices: Sarajevo assassination, July Crisis, war begins, U.S. entry, armistice
U.S. entry, Sarajevo assassination, war begins, armistice, July Crisis
War begins, armistice, July Crisis, Sarajevo assassination, U.S. entry
July Crisis, armistice, Sarajevo assassination, war begins, U.S. entry
activities.correctAnswer: Sarajevo assassination, July Crisis, war begins, U.S. entry, armistice
activities.feedback: That order shows the outbreak first, then later widening and ending. If one item feels out of place, check whether it belongs at the start, during the war, or at the end.
